title: A face-isolation proof of the two-variable Gaussian Moments Conjecture
summary: Let $(X,Y)$ be independent standard real Gaussian random variables, and let $(P\in\mathbb C[X,Y])$ satisfy $\mathbb E!\left(P(X,Y)^m\right)=0$ for every $(m\ge1)$. Using the complex coordinates $Z=\frac{X+iY}{\sqrt2}, \qquad W=\frac{X-iY}{\sqrt2},$ we prove that the monomial support of $(P)$ is strictly one-sided with respect to the weight $\operatorname{wt}(Z^aW^b)=a-b$. Thus either every monomial occurring in $(P)$ has positive weight, or every monomial has negative weight.
